Based on Sans Famille by Hector Malot

Tells the story of Remi who is sold off to Vitalis the travelling musician and his band of performing animals.

One day Kan-chan finds a magic bottle in the attic. Whenever someone sneezes, a genie named Hakushon Daimaou is brought out and must grant any wish of whoever sneezed until he or she sneezes again. Sometimes, however, he accidentally fails and only causes trouble instead of granting any wishes.

Atsuko "Akko-chan" Kagami (known variously as "Stilly," "Caroline," or "Julie" in Western versions of the anime) is an energetic elementary school girl who has an affinity for mirrors. One day, her favorite mirror which was given to Akko by her mother (or in some versions, by her father, as a present from India) is broken, and she prefers to bury it in her yard rather than throw it to the trash can. In her dreams, she is contacted by a spirit (or in some cases the Queen of the Mirror Kingdom) who is moved that the little girl would treat the mirror so respectfully and not simply throw it away. Akko-chan is then given the gift of a magical mirror and taught an enchantment that will allow her to transform into anything she wishes.

(Source: Wikipedia)

A dog race is interrupted by a ringmaster, who attaches fish to the dog’s collars and makes them run in circles. The crowd is incensed, but the ringmaster insists that the audience is no better off than the dogs. In the end the ringmaster is assassinated and the race continues, but a single red rose sprouts from the ringmaster’s blood; a symbol of truth in a crazy world?

-AniDB

Very loosely based upon the Moomin books by Finnish author Tove Jansson. Jansson, however, never really approved of the series due to dramatic changes in plot, atmosphere, character personality, appearance and names etc. The series was directed to adults rather than children.

(Source: Wikipedia)
A Japanese version of an old 15th century French song 'Sur le Pont d'Avignon,' which describes how people would come and dance on the Pont St. Bénézet (Pont d’Avignon).

Kozue is a high school girl and an enthusiastic volleyball player. Her dream is to play on the Japanese national volleyball team. Over the course of the series she makes it from the school district league up to the Japanese volleyball finals, step by step until the international volleyball championship. But the faster and higher Kozue climbs, the more she is confronted with the dark side of success: too-high expectations, self-conceit, and envy.

(Source: Anime News Network)

title.romaji: Attack No.1: Namida no Kaiten Receive
Attack No.1: Namida no Sekai Senshuken

media.description:
The Japanese team have been selected to compete in the World Junior Championships. Kozue, Midori, Kakinouchi and the other all-Japan teams, under coach Inokuma, work hard on rigorous training and head for New York, where the world's strongest players await.

In the first round the team was immediately overwhelmed by the outstanding stamina of the American players, but the team managed. The final match has finally arrived. In order to defeat the spikes of the Soviet team, Kozue and her team devised a secret plan. Where will the glory shine? The time of the decisive battle is approaching.

Returning home from an ocean trip, young Isamu meets the beautiful sea-dweller Angel on a volcanic island. Attacked by a fiery dragon, Isamu and Angel escape on the observation boat See Through, and Angel invites Isamu to see her undersea kingdom of Atlas.

(Source: AniDB)

The non-athletic head of the school newspaper department participates in various club activities, including a number of sports clubs, with disastrously hilarious results.

(Source: AniDB)
A surrealistic short from minimalist cartoonist Kuri Yoji.
Akira, a young detective, uses his Invisibility to investigate a case where the Mona Lisa has been stolen by the villainous Team Z.

This is an animated version of Yanase Takashi's picture book featuring the friendship between a mother dog, Muku-muku, who lost her puppy, and the baby lion Buru-buru, who lost her mother. Although Tezuka Osamu planned to create an entire musical animated series for this story focused on the feelings of the mother dog and baby lion, this animated production was the only one never completed.

(Source: en.tezuka.co.jp)

Note: In 1998, a renewed version was produced that changed some dialogue and re-recorded the audio with new voice actors. The last scene was also modified.

Hanako-chan, a flower loving person, encounters a mole in her garden and wonders what would happen if the moles could be trained to assist in gardening. Then her idea goes with the wind...

Based on a manga of Akatsuka Fujio.

Batsugoro was the owner of a grocery store, Yaobatsu. When he tried to take a balloon hanged caught on the branch for a little child, he fell on to the ground to die. His son, Ataro, succeeded to the store, but Batsugoro was worried about him, and he remained there being a ghost. Ataro managed the shop alone, but soon his follower, Dekoppachi, began to help him. Being surrounded by strange characters such as, Nyarome, Butamatsu, the heart-warming story develops.

(Source: AnimeNfo)

media.description:
A puppy, Poko, jumps out of a refrigerator and takes a boy, Misuke, to an ice world full of adventure through the refrigerator. In the ice world, there is a girl called Nally who wants warm food. So they try to find some warm food for her, but everything freezes so quickly in the ice world...

(Source: Official Website, edited)

Note: First promotional film made to attract new students to Yahama's electronic organ classes.

Hikoichi and Osato, who are selling the many watermelons they harvested, in front of the castle, happen to meet a chief counselor named Chuemon. Chuemon was at his wits end because a messenger from a neighboring country had come to him with an unreasonable demand and he was looking for someone wise and intelligent to help him. Hikoichi agrees to help him, on the condition that Chuemon buys all of the watermelons if Hikoichi can win a battle of wits. Hikoichi makes seemingly impossible problems possible using his wits and unconventional methods. This drama rhythmically progresses with wisdom and courage.

This film won Gold in the Tokyo Educational Film Competition.

(Source: Sukugawa International Short Film Festival)

The Japanese version of the 1880 Neapolitan song Funiculì funiculà, originally composed by Luigi Denza, with lyrics from Peppino Turco. A Japanese rendition of the song performed by Japanese vocal group Duke Aces was originally broadcast on NHK's Minna no Uta program in April 1961. It was released under the title Tozandensha (Mountain Railway) and was accompanied by shadow play from the Kakashiza Shadow Play Theatre. It is believed to now be lost media.

In June 1970, a performance of the song by the Osaka Sumiyoshi Boys and Girls Choir (Osaka Sumiyoshi Shounen Shoujo Gasshoudan) was broadcast on the Minna no Uta program, this time using the original song title.

Zen-chan Tsuu-chan is a Japanese educational anime series produced by Jiho Eigasha. It was aired in October 20th, 1969 until January 17th, 1970 on Nippon TV. Each episode is 5 minutes long. The show is considered a lost media.

A boy takes a walk outside as he notices little bits of spring starts to appear. Though in the end, it turns out he is merely dreaming it and winter is at its peak.

The music video was re-aired after 44 years due to being lost media. The Minna no Uta Hakkutsu Project (Minna no Uta Excavation Project) was able to find discover a copy of the original audio, as only the animated footage was originally saved by the NHK in the 70s.
